questions.q: A projectile is launched with speed 20 m/s at an angle of 30° with the horizontal. What is the maximum height reached by the projectile? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.a: Correct answer: 5 m. Steps: u = 20 m/s, θ = 30°, sin30° = 0.5. H = (u² sin²θ)/(2g) = (400 × 0.25)/(20) = 100/20 = 5 m. A wrong answer (e.g., 10 m or 2.5 m) reveals the student either forgot the factor of 2 in the denominator, used sinθ instead of sin²θ, or confused the range formula with the height formula.

questions.q: Two projectiles are launched with the same initial speed u. Projectile A is launched at angle θ, and Projectile B at angle (90° - θ). Without calculating, explain why both have the same horizontal range. What happens to their maximum heights?
questions.a: Correct answer: Range formula R = (u² sin2θ)/g depends on sin2θ. For complementary angles, 2(90°-θ) = 180°-2θ, and sin(180°-2θ) = sin2θ, so ranges are equal. Maximum heights are H_A = (u² sin²θ)/(2g) and H_B = (u² cos²θ)/(2g), which are different unless θ = 45°. A wrong answer reveals the student memorizes "complementary angles give same range" without understanding the trigonometric reason, or thinks heights are also equal.

questions.q: A stone is projected from ground level with speed 25 m/s at an angle of 37° (sin37° = 0.6, cos37° = 0.8). Calculate: (a) maximum height, (b) horizontal range, (c) time of flight. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.a:
(a) H = (u² sin²θ)/(2g) = (625 × 0.36)/20 = 225/20 = 11.25 m
(b) R = (u² sin2θ)/g = (625 × 2 × 0.6 × 0.8)/10 = (625 × 0.96)/10 = 600/10 = 60 m
(c) T = 2u sinθ/g = (2 × 25 × 0.6)/10 = 30/10 = 3 s
A wrong answer reveals unit inconsistency (e.g., forgetting to square u), using sinθ instead of sin2θ for range, or confusing time of flight with time to max height.

questions.q: A projectile has a maximum range of 100 m on level ground. What is the maximum height it can reach when launched at 45°? If the same projectile is launched at 30°, what will be its range? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.a: At 45°, R_max = u²/g = 100 m → u² = 1000 m²/s². H_max at 45° = (u² sin²45°)/(2g) = (1000 × 0.5)/20 = 25 m. At 30°, R = (u² sin60°)/g = (1000 × √3/2)/10 = 50√3 ≈ 86.6 m. A wrong answer (e.g., H = 50 m or R = 50 m) reveals the student doesn't connect R_max to u²/g, or uses sin30° instead of sin60° in the range formula.

questions.q: A student claims: "If I double the launch speed, the maximum height becomes double, and the range also becomes double." Evaluate this claim using the formulas. Provide a counterexample with numbers.
questions.a: Claim is FALSE. H ∝ u² and R ∝ u², so doubling speed quadruples both height and range. Counterexample: u = 10 m/s, θ = 30°, g = 10 m/s² → H = 1.25 m, R = 5√3 ≈ 8.66 m. Double speed to 20 m/s → H = 5 m (4×), R = 20√3 ≈ 34.64 m (4×). A wrong evaluation reveals the student thinks formulas are linear in u, not quadratic.

questions.q: Design a simple experiment using a water hose and a measuring tape to verify that the maximum range of a water jet occurs at 45° projection angle. What measurements would you take, and how would you account for the height of the hose nozzle above ground?
questions.a: Good answer: Fix water pressure constant. Measure horizontal distance where water hits ground for angles 15°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 75°. Plot range vs angle; peak should be near 45°. Account for nozzle height h by using R = (u cosθ/g)[u sinθ + √(u²sin²θ + 2gh)] instead of level-ground formula. Poor answer ignores nozzle height or assumes speed is same at all angles without verifying constant pressure.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The maximum height (H) of a projectile is the highest vertical position reached above the launch point, given by H = (u² sin²θ)/(2g), where u is the initial speed, θ is the projection angle with horizontal, and g is ______ due to gravity.
Fill in the blank: Observe a cricket ball thrown during a match — it rises to a peak height before falling back to the ground at some ______ from the bowler.

Fill in the blank: The maximum height (H) of a projectile is the highest vertical position reached above the launch point, given by H = (u² sin²θ)/(______g), where u is the initial speed, θ is the projection angle with horizontal, and g is acceleration due to gravity.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can derive the formulas for maximum height and range from the trajectory equation or kinematic equations, calculate these quantities for given launch parameters, and explain why complementary angles yield the same range.
